Generated by `experiments/generate_amendment_history.py` on 2026-10-22 at commit 342c62d-dirty from the git log, configs/registered_rules.json; do not edit by hand.

Every change to a registered rule since the baseline, taken from `Amends:` trailers in the git log. Edits to this file are overwritten by the next run; change a commit message, or add a trailer to a new commit, instead.

**Baseline.** `docs/preregistration_baseline_2026-10-15.md` is the registration exactly as it stood at the freeze of 15 October 2026, SHA-256 `08b02e8d303b61b4ebb4452266e54241c153b2600d58039bb5bb70dbb5e14104`, and is never edited. Amendments before that date are the in-document list inside the baseline itself; they were made before this mechanism existed and are not reconstructed here, because the commits of that period carry no trailers and a reconstruction would assert dates the log cannot support.

**Current values** live in `configs/registered_rules.json` (10 rules) and are asserted against the implementation by `tests/test_registration_matches_the_code.py`. This file says how they got there; that file says they are still true.

## Amendments

### 2026-10-22 — `tested_models`

- **From** confirmatory_v2_message_passing_noisy_or and confirmatory_v2_linear_response_noisy_or, each at one-sided 0.025 **to** confirmatory_v2_linear_response_noisy_or
- Governs: One model: the noisy-OR configuration of the linear-response encoder. The sigmoid head was dropped on 15 October 2026 because only noisy-OR has modules that can be read as pathways; the message-passing encoder moved to robustness_models on 22 October 2026 (the owner: "Defer it to robustness. I don't want it constraining things because this is more about mechanistically identifiably predictive nosology"). The registered reason is that only the linear-response encoder has a closed-form steady state, so only there can the sensitivity of a label to a sign-disputed edge, and hence whether a disputed sign is identifiable at all, be read without a training run. With one tested model the familywise chance of a lucky pass is the level the model is tested at, so the 0.05 of the two-model arithmetic is no longer claimed and alpha_one_sided is now conservative by a factor of two; raising it is a separate amendment the owner has not taken (decision 9.77).
- Commit `342c62d9b156`: Defer the message-passing encoder to a robustness reading

### 2026-10-22 — `robustness_models`

- **From** no such rule; a robustness reading of an encoder was not registered **to** confirmatory_v2_message_passing_noisy_or
- Governs: Read and reported with their intervals outside the tested family, spending no alpha, as the two permutation readings have since 8 October 2026. The message-passing encoder sits here from 22 October 2026 so a conclusion of the tested model can be checked against a second encoder of a different inductive bias without that check constraining the registered family. A robustness reading that disagrees is reported as a disagreement and cannot withdraw the tested model's result; the corroboration a second tested model would have given is therefore given up, which is the cost the owner accepted.
- Commit `342c62d9b156`: Defer the message-passing encoder to a robustness reading
